chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar concerning the supplication for the child, he said:

"Pour a bucket of Zamzam water, then enter the House. When you stand at the door of the House, take hold of the door ring, then say: 'O Allah, indeed the House is Your House and the servant is Your servant, and You have said, "And whoever enters it is secure," so secure me from Your punishment and save me from Your wrath.' Then enter the House and pray two rak'ahs on the red marble."

Then proceed to the pillar opposite the Stone, and press your chest against it, then say: 'O One, O Noble, O Near, O Distant, O Mighty, O Wise: "Do not leave me solitary, and You are the best of inheritors." "Grant me from Yourself a good offspring, indeed You are the Hearer of supplication."'

Then circle the pillar, pressing your back and stomach against it, and supplicate with this supplication; if Allah wills something, it will be.' And it is not permissible for a person to pray the obligatory prayer in the Ka'bah when choosing, but it is permissible in case of necessity and fear of missing the time. Narrated.
11 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: "The obligatory prayer is not prayed in the Ka'bah, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not enter the Ka'bah during a pilgrimage or a visitation, but he entered it during the Conquest - the Conquest of Mecca - and prayed two rak'ahs between the two pillars, with him was Usamah ibn Zayd."

key_terms.الرُّخَامَةِ الْحَمْرَاءِ: The red marble, a specific stone inside the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.زَمْزَمَ: Zamzam water, sacred water from the well in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and legal ruling for entering and praying inside the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi, details the specific devotional practices for entering the Ka'bah, including the ritual use of Zamzam water and touching the door ring, while grounding the legal ruling in the Prophetic precedent that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) did not perform obligatory prayers inside during Hajj or Umrah. The text clarifies that the prohibition of offering fard prayers within the Ka'bah is for those with the choice (ikhtiyar), permitting it only under necessity (idtirar) or fear of missing the prayer time, a distinction rooted in the Prophet's entry during the Conquest of Mecca where he prayed two rak'ahs between the pillars. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between voluntary supererogatory acts and obligatory duties within the sacred sanctuary.
